title: The Burning Man
text: A man walks toward you along the road, on fire from head to foot, quite calm. The flames do not seem to eat him; they only keep him company. He stops a polite distance away, smoke curling from his collar, and asks if anyone has water.

options.label: The one the tides favor goes to him with water, hoping to quench what burns him.

outcomes.text: The flames gutter out. He thanks them in a voice like a cooling coal, promising to remember the favor.
The flames will not go out. Instead they leap gladly up the sleeve that reached for him while he watches with polite interest.

options.label: Pass by and keep the water. A man who does not burn needs no help from you.

outcomes.text: He walks on without another word. The grass behind him smokes for an hour.
